body.heading: About this sheet
paragraphs: Free SparkKindly Kids writing & tracing printable: Pattern Practice 01.
Dotted lines, letters and numbers to trace slowly and carefully, building the hand control that handwriting grows from.

body.heading: How to use it
paragraphs: Print the sheet, sit at a table with feet flat, and trace each dotted line from the dot. Slow and steady beats fast and scribbly.

takeaway: Tracing grows the small hand muscles and the confidence every young writer needs.
materials: A chunky pencil or crayon that is easy to grip
supervision: Sit alongside for the first row, then let them show you the rest — praise effort and wobbly lines alike.
safetyNotes: A short, thick pencil is easier and safer for small hands than a long sharp one.
Print at 100% size (not "fit to page") so the sheet keeps its true size and the pictures stay the size they were drawn.
screenFreeExtension: Hide letters or numbers around the room on sticky notes and send your tracer on a hunt to find and copy each one.
